description: cc-review brain (target spec): deterministic, zero-tolerance PR/MR review as one self-contained workflow. First-vs-re-run is decided by the bot's overview-comment marker. FIRST review: opus holistic review posts the overview (diff-first), two web-backed research agents (ai-slop + general) + memories/docs + static tools gather context, a difficulty-scaled squad reviews, JS dedup + one check agent filters false positives, deterministic verdict, post, memory.   tsx /tmp/cc-review-bot/scripts/review-platform.ts post-overview --pr 15 --body-file .cc-run/cc-answer.md
Report the comment id. Markdown:
<<<MD
The diff raises the job-level timeout from 30 to 60 minutes in both cc-review.yml and cc-review-inter…

summary: cc-review brain (target spec): deterministic, zero-tolerance PR/MR review as one self-contained workflow. First-vs-re-run is decided by the bot's overview-comment marker. FIRST review: opus holistic review posts the overview (diff-first), two web-backed research agents (ai-slop + general) + memories/docs + static tools gather context, a difficulty-scaled squad reviews, JS dedup + one check agent filters false positives, deterministic verdict, post, memory. RE-RUN: a hard 'first finish prev review' gate (ping overrides), comment management with resolve-with-message, then a significant-change check (JS prefilter + agent) decides whether to redraw the overview in place and re-research; the squad re-reviews either way. A small review-state marker (head sha + file count) records what was last reviewed for that check. Posting gated on post===true.

The workflow completed. Here is its return value verbatim as JSON:

```json
{"ok":true,"mode":"answer","answer":"The diff raises the job-level timeout from 30 to 60 minutes in both cc-review.yml and cc-review-interactive.yml. The commenter is making an analytical observation about the risk: doubling the ceiling doubles the worst-case billable runner time per review, and the change does not address the underlying cause of slowness in the runtime-clone pipeline. A genuinely hung job now runs for up to 60 minutes before GitHub cancels it instead of 30.","posted":true}
```
